<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Tenancy\Runtime\Internal\Bootstrappers;

use CoreX\Config\Exceptions\InvalidConfiguration;
use CoreX\Context\Data\DatabaseConnectionConfig;
use CoreX\Context\Data\TenantContext;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Runtime\Contracts\TenantBootstrapper;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Runtime\Internal\FrameworkConfig;
use Illuminate\Cache\CacheManager;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
use Illuminate\Filesystem\Filesystem;
use Illuminate\Session\SessionManager;
use Illuminate\Session\Store;
use Override;
use SessionHandlerInterface;

/**
 * Moves the live session handler to the account: database connection, per-account cache
 * prefix (redis/memcached), per-account directory (file). The Store object held by the
 * request, `session.store` and the auth guards stays the same; only its handler and the
 * session config change, and both are restored on revert (stored sessions are not deleted).
 */
final class SessionConnectionBootstrapper implements TenantBootstrapper
{
    public const array SUPPORTED_DRIVERS = ['database', 'redis', 'memcached', 'file'];

    /** @var array<array-key, mixed>|null */
    private ?array $original = null;

    /** @var array<string, SessionHandlerInterface> */
    private array $handlers = [];

    /** @var array<array-key, mixed>|null */
    private ?array $cacheOriginal = null;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly SessionManager $sessions,
        private readonly CacheManager $cache,
        private readonly Container $container,
        private readonly FrameworkConfig $config,
        private readonly string $centralConnection,
        private readonly Filesystem $files,
    ) {}

    #[Override]
    public function bootstrap(TenantContext $context, DatabaseConnectionConfig $database): void
    {
        $this->original = (array) $this->config->get('session');
        $driver = $this->original['driver'] ?? null;

        if ($driver === null) {
            return;
        }

        if (! in_array($driver, self::SUPPORTED_DRIVERS, true)) {
            throw new InvalidConfiguration(['corex-tenancy.session: unsupported driver']);
        }

        foreach ($this->createdStores() as $name => $store) {
            $this->handlers[$name] = $store->getHandler();
        }

        $suffix = hash('sha256', $context->account->id);

        if ($driver === 'database') {
            $this->config->set('session.connection', 'tenant');
        } elseif ($driver === 'file') {
            $root = $this->original['files'] ?? null;

            if (! is_string($root) || $root === '') {
                throw new InvalidConfiguration(['corex-tenancy.session.files: file sessions need a directory']);
            }

            $path = rtrim($root, '/').'/corex-tenants/'.$suffix;
            $this->files->ensureDirectoryExists($path, 0700, true);

            if (! $this->files->isDirectory($path) || ! $this->files->isWritable($path)) {
                throw new InvalidConfiguration(['corex-tenancy.session.files: directory is not writable']);
            }

            $this->config->set('session.files', $path);
        } else {
            $name = $this->original['store'] ?? null;

            if (! is_string($name) || $name === '') {
                throw new InvalidConfiguration(['corex-tenancy.session.store: required for redis/memcached sessions']);
            }

            $this->cacheOriginal = (array) $this->config->get("cache.stores.{$name}");
            $existing = $this->cacheOriginal['prefix'] ?? $this->config->get('cache.prefix', '');
            $prefix = 'corex-session:'.$suffix.':'.(is_string($existing) ? $existing : '');
            $this->config->set("cache.stores.{$name}.prefix", $prefix);

            if ($driver === 'redis') {
                $this->config->set('session.prefix', $prefix); // Laravel otherwise overrides the cache prefix
            }

            $this->cache->forgetDriver($name);
        }

        // Keep the Store object held by request/session.store/Auth; replace its handler.
        // A fresh manager respects database, cache clone, Redis connection/prefix and file settings.
        $created = $this->createdStores();

        if (isset($created[$driver])) {
            $created[$driver]->setHandler($this->freshHandler($driver));
        }
    }

    #[Override]
    public function revert(): void
    {
        if ($this->original === null) {
            return;
        }

        $this->config->set('session', $this->original);

        if ($this->cacheOriginal !== null) {
            $name = $this->original['store'];
            \assert(\is_string($name));
            $this->config->set("cache.stores.{$name}", $this->cacheOriginal);
            $this->cache->forgetDriver($name);
        }

        // The connection bootstrapper reverts later, so a null connection must resolve explicitly to central here.
        if (($this->original['driver'] ?? null) === 'database') {
            $this->config->set('session.connection', $this->original['connection'] ?? $this->centralConnection);
        }

        foreach ($this->createdStores() as $name => $store) {
            $store->setHandler($this->handlers[$name] ?? $this->freshHandler($name));
        }

        $this->config->set('session', $this->original);
        $this->original = null;
        $this->handlers = [];
        $this->cacheOriginal = null;
    }

    /** @return array<string, Store> */
    private function createdStores(): array
    {
        /** @var array<string, Store> $stores */
        $stores = $this->sessions->getDrivers();

        return $stores;
    }

    private function freshHandler(string $driver): SessionHandlerInterface
    {
        /** @var Store $store */
        $store = (new SessionManager($this->container))->driver($driver);

        return $store->getHandler();
    }
}

1→# P07.3 — impersonation profiles and committed dual audit

Status: GREEN. Base commit `9f428a7c81a20c1948f21f20c4b6ad54b6fa9fe1`; product commit `e7917772` (`candidate-commit.txt`). The second commit carries only execution evidence and plan bookkeeping because post-commit contract guards, the candidate SHA, and the independent review must be recorded after the product anchor exists.

The kernel now provides `SynchronousAuditWriter` and its committed database implementation. Tenancy uses `ImpersonationGrantStore` and `ImpersonationAuditSink`, an atomic profile-aware claim, and a central-first/tenant-second sink. The `standard` profile is the default; `regulated` requires a staff approver in the claim predicate; `dev` requires production acknowledgement. Audit failure denies `start`, leaves no impersonation session, and consumes the grant. A tenant mirror failure retains the committed central intent under D100. The scoped write guard restores its allowance after nested calls and exceptions. The runtime globals baseline is `{}`.

Validation: 27 profile matrix cells / 55 assertions; focused impersonation 40 passed / 172 assertions; stock writer 2 passed; full tenancy 589 passed, 6 existing Redis skips / 2200 assertions; root PG 242 passed / 1156 assertions; all 21 package suites passed. Runtime globals positive and injected `now()` negative passed. Removed `require_approved_by` grep is empty. PHP API write twice was byte identical and its check passed; full BC check passed with two exact D96/D100 `ImpersonationPolicy` approvals against the accepted historical base. Golden passed 4 snapshots / 1440 assertions with 11 added, zero removed and 4 changed semantic entries. Root lint, analyse, anti-weakening, package docs, configuration reference, and both post-commit contract guards passed. Logs and the semantic delta are in this directory.

The product commit includes the generated public API reference, configuration metadata, removal of stale PHPStan baseline entries, exact BC approvals, and formatting of two older P07 proof scripts needed for the root lint gate. Golden rebaseline documentation records the P07.3 change. These supporting files are tied to the declared package surfaces and validation.

The systemic invariant model and adversarial self-check are in `../P07.3/invariant-model.md` and `../P07.3/self-check.json`.

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Contracts;

use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Data\ClaimedGrant;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Data\GrantClaim;

#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Implement, since: '1.0')]
interface ImpersonationGrantStore
{
    public function claim(GrantClaim $claim): ?ClaimedGrant;

    public function claimedReason(string $grantId): ?string;
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Audit\Enums;

use CoreX\Attributes\Api;

/**
 * Who performed an audited change (sys_audit_log CHECK constraint).
 *
 * `Support` (D137) — a staff identity acting under B-11 §5.9 impersonation;
 * added additively (`sys_audit_actor_ck`/`mod_ll_actor_ck` both widened by
 * new migrations, never by editing the closed P1.8/P1.3 files).
 */
#[Api(since: '1.0')]
enum ActorType: string
{
    case User = 'user';
    case Agent = 'agent';
    case ApiKey = 'api_key';
    case System = 'system';
    case Support = 'support';
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Contracts;

use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Data\ImpersonationAuditEvent;

#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Implement, since: '1.0')]
interface ImpersonationAuditSink
{
    /** Throw when persistence or commit is uncertain. */
    public function record(ImpersonationAuditEvent $event): void;
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Data;

use CoreX\Attributes\Api;
use DateTimeImmutable;

#[Api(since: '1.0')]
final readonly class ClaimedGrant
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $grantId,
        public ?string $targetUserId,
        public string $reason,
        public DateTimeImmutable $expiresAt,
    ) {}
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Data;

use CoreX\Attributes\Api;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Enums\ImpersonationProfile;
use DateTimeImmutable;

#[Api(since: '1.0')]
final readonly class ImpersonationAuditEvent
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $event,
        public string $accountId,
        public string $grantId,
        public string $staffIdentityId,
        public string $targetUserId,
        public string $reason,
        public ImpersonationProfile $profile,
        public DateTimeImmutable $occurredAt,
        public ?DateTimeImmutable $expiresAt = null,
    ) {}
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Internal\Models;

use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

/**
 * `root_impersonation_grants` — thin Eloquent read model. The registrar
 * supplies the configured central connection when resolving an instance;
 * callers of Eloquent's static API must select that connection explicitly.
 * The one-time atomic claim itself is a query-builder `UPDATE` in
 * {@see CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Internal\DatabaseImpersonationGrantStore} (D143),
 * not an Eloquent write — this model exists for the L2 exempt-list
 * (`ImpersonatedModelWriteGuard`) and read access after the claim.
 *
 * @property string $id
 * @property string $staff_identity_id
 * @property string $account_id
 * @property ?string $target_user_id
 * @property string $reason
 * @property ?string $approved_by
 * @property CarbonImmutable $expires_at
 * @property ?CarbonImmutable $used_at
 * @property ?CarbonImmutable $revoked_at
 * @property CarbonImmutable $created_at
 * @property CarbonImmutable $updated_at
 */
final class ImpersonationGrant extends Model
{
    protected $table = 'root_impersonation_grants';

    protected $guarded = [];

    /** @return array<string, string> */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'expires_at' => 'immutable_datetime',
            'used_at' => 'immutable_datetime',
            'revoked_at' => 'immutable_datetime',
        ];
    }
}

1→# P07.3 impersonation invariant model

Risk class: auth, transaction, data integrity. PostgreSQL is the supported grant and audit driver.

| Operation | Resource | Invariant and enforcement | Interference path | Evidence |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Claim | Central `root_impersonation_grants` | One `UPDATE ... WHERE` checks unused, unrevoked, unexpired, nonempty reason, staff claimant, profile TTL, and regulated independent staff approver. An ambient central transaction is refused. | Two concurrent claimants serialize on the grant row; only one can update `used_at` from null. | `ImpersonationProfileTest` 27 cells; existing one-use flow test. |
| Start audit | Central `root_account_events` | Commit the event before any tenant mirror or login. Failure denies access; the claim stays used. | Central insert/commit can fail or have uncertain outcome. It is never rolled back by later tenant failure. | `ImpersonationAuditTest` central failure and tenant failure. |
| Tenant mirror | Tenant `sys_audit_log` | Standard and regulated use the stock `SynchronousAuditWriter`, which requires an event snapshot, rejects ambient transactions and commits before returning. Dev omits this mirror. Optional `AuditLogger` and queue settings have no effect. | Tenant insert/commit can fail after central intent commits; login stays closed. | Core writer persistence/transaction tests; tenancy stock writer and failure tests. |
10→| Session/login | Current request session and auth guard | Start records audit before setting impersonation keys and calling login. Login failure clears auth/session before failed audit. Stop clears auth/session before ended audit. | Audit failure cannot leave an opened impersonation session; a failed login leaves a consumed grant. | `ImpersonationTest`, `ImpersonationAuditTest`. |
| Write guard | Scoped guard instance | Only the current instance may temporarily permit an intentional model write; nested calls restore the previous value after exceptions. | Another scoped instance and later requests remain closed. | `ImpersonationWriteGuardTest`. |

No cross-database atomic commit is claimed. Central intent describes the attempted access and can remain without a tenant row after failure (PLAN3.D100). The later schema baseline migration belongs to P08.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Identity\Laravel;

use CoreX\Access\Access\Laravel\PrincipalIdentity;
use CoreX\Access\Enums\PrincipalType;
use CoreX\Access\Laravel\AuthOptions;
use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Context\Contracts\IdentityPasswordRehasher;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\UserProvider;
use Illuminate\Database\Query\Builder;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Override;
use SensitiveParameter;

/**
 * The boxed-and-cloud login lane's own {@see UserProvider} (D125, OQ-18
 * variant A): reads a users-shaped table through query-builder, entirely by
 * {@see AuthOptions} identity fields — connection/table/column names — so
 * `axiomasoft/corex-access` never imports a model from `axiomasoft/corex-tenancy` (AC-28). Every
 * lookup goes through {@see query()}, which always applies the "live user"
 * filter (active = true AND deleted_at IS NULL): without it in
 * retrieveById() too, a session survives the very deactivation meant to end
 * it.
 *
 * `retrieveByToken()`/`updateRememberToken()` are permanent no-ops: the
 * frozen `users` DDL (P2.7, D125) carries no `remember_token` column and one
 * is not being added — "remember me" is simply unsupported by this
 * provider.
 */
#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Call, since: '1.0')]
final class PrincipalUserProvider implements UserProvider
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly AuthOptions $options,
    ) {}

    #[Override]
    public function retrieveById($identifier): ?Authenticatable
    {
        $row = $this->query()->where($this->idColumn(), $identifier)->first();

        return $this->toPrincipal($row);
    }

    /**
     * No `remember_token` column exists on the configured table (frozen
     * DB_SCHEMA) — remember-me sessions are not supported.
     */
    #[Override]
    public function retrieveByToken($identifier, #[SensitiveParameter] mixed $token): ?Authenticatable
    {
        return null;
    }

    /** No-op — see {@see retrieveByToken()}. */
    #[Override]
    public function updateRememberToken(Authenticatable $user, #[SensitiveParameter] mixed $token): void
    {
        // Intentionally empty: no remember_token column to persist into.
    }

    /** @param  array<string, mixed>  $credentials */
    #[Override]
    public function retrieveByCredentials(#[SensitiveParameter] array $credentials): ?Authenticatable
    {
        $email = $credentials['email'] ?? null;

        if (! is_string($email) || $email === '') {
            return null;
        }

        // The `password` key is never used to build the WHERE (Laravel canon,
        // validated separately by validateCredentials()); the unique index on
        // this schema is `lower(email)`, so the match is case-insensitive.
        $row = $this->query()
            ->whereRaw('lower('.$this->emailColumn().') = ?', [mb_strtolower($email)])
            ->first();

        return $this->toPrincipal($row);
    }

    /** @param  array<string, mixed>  $credentials */
    #[Override]
    public function validateCredentials(Authenticatable $user, #[SensitiveParameter] array $credentials): bool

1→# axiomasoft/corex-tenancy

Laravel tenancy primitives for CoreX's physical PostgreSQL database-per-account
profile.

## Support impersonation

Enable the OIDC impersonation lane with `corex-tenancy.oidc.impersonation.enabled`.
Choose `corex-tenancy.impersonation.profile`: `standard` (default, 60-minute maximum grant),
10→`regulated` (30 minutes and approval by a different staff identity), or `dev` (480 minutes).
Production `dev` requires `corex.acknowledged_dangerous_modes` to contain
`corex-tenancy.impersonation.profile`. All grants are claimed once atomically and must carry a
reason. `standard` and `regulated` commit correlated central and tenant audit rows before login;
`dev` commits central audit only. Any audit failure denies access and leaves the grant consumed.
The central intent remains if the tenant mirror fails. Hosts may implement
`ImpersonationGrantStore` and `ImpersonationAuditSink`; a custom sink must preserve committed,
fail-closed writes. The current scoped `ImpersonatedModelWriteGuard` instance provides
`allowing()` for a deliberately permitted write.

20→## Optional wakeup root hints

`corex-tenancy.wakeup.driver` defaults to `local_sweep`. With `axiomasoft/corex-wakeup` installed, a cloud
deployment may explicitly select `root_registry`; this enables the advisory `root_wakeup_hints`
table and the `corex:tenancy:wakeup-root-sweep` command. Hints never replace a tenant-local request or
provide authority to select an account connection.

## Package engine and configuration

CoreX owns the account/domain models, physical tenancy engine and synchronous golden-template
30→provisioning. Account identifiers use UUIDv7; account fields are explicit typed columns. The legacy
`root_accounts.data` column is no longer used for model attributes. Existing signup claim and pool
cleanup SQL still use it for idempotency and crash recovery until P08 (D107); retain the column and
these writes until that migration is complete. Saved/deleting model events invalidate the central host cache.

Publish configuration with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=corex-tenancy-config`. All settings,
including wakeup, use `config/corex-tenancy.php` under `corex-tenancy`. Migrate host overrides from the
previous `tenancy` key; the old key and model/provider configuration knobs have been removed.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI.
